ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is an inscribed quadrilateral of the circle $\odot O$. If $\angle BOD = 70^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle C$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle BOD=70^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle A=\frac{1}{2}\angle BOD=35^\circ$,\\
since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in circle $\odot O$,\\
it follows that $\angle C+\angle A=180^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle C=\boxed{145^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a circle, with the center labeled O. A is on the left side of the circle, B is at the upper right, D is at the lower right, and C is located on the smaller arc BD on the right side. Line segments OB and OD connect from the center of the circle to B and D, forming the central angle ∠BOD. All four vertices of quadrilateral ABCD are on the circle. Then reason: ∠BOD = 70° is the central angle corresponding to the minor arc BD, so the measure of the minor arc BD is 70°. Since C is on the minor arc BD, ∠C, that is, ∠BCD, intercepts the major arc BD on the other side. Major arc BD = 360° - 70° = 290°. According to the inscribed angle theorem, an inscribed angle is equal to half the measure of the arc it subtends, so ∠C = 290° / 2 = 145°.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a circle with center O, with B and D on the right side and C located on the minor arc between B and D. The angle sought is the inscribed angle ∠BCD, whose sides pass through B and D; since C lies on the minor arc BD, ∠C intercepts the opposite major arc BD. From the text, ∠BOD = 70°, so the minor arc BD measures 70° and the major arc BD measures 360° − 70° = 290°. Apply the inscribed-angle theorem: ∠C = half its intercepted arc = 290°/2 = 145°.
